column1: # CLOSED INVENTORY of every file this branch changed, and how each is covered.
# scripts/test-doc-evidence-coverage.sh reverts one fix at a time and counts the controls
# that notice. It printed "every fix has a control". It mutated ONE FILE —
# scripts/check_doc_evidence.py — from a hand-maintained list of replacements. Fixes in
# gate-receipts.sh, test-doc-evidence.sh, the Makefile and the CI workflow were outside
# its target entirely and could be reverted with nothing going red. MUTATION-DEAD catches
# a LISTED replacement that stops applying; an OMITTED one is invisible, and the whole
# point of that runner was to catch a control that silently stops testing.
# So the denominator is no longer a string in a script. It comes from git — the set of
# files this branch changed against its merge-base with main — and is reconciled against
# this file IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, exactly as tests/conformance-manifest.txt is reconciled
#   a changed file with no row here          -> UNDECLARED  (fail)
#   a row here naming an unchanged file      -> MISSING     (fail)
#   a `mutated` row with no mutation         -> UNCOVERED   (fail)
#   a mutation whose patch no longer applies -> DEAD        (fail)
# A file cannot leave the measurement by being forgotten; it can only leave by being
# argued for in a row here, which is a reviewed edit.
# Columns are TAB-separated: path  disposition  note
#   mutated            the coverage runner reverts fixes in this file and requires
#                      controls to go red. Every such file must have >=1 mutation.
#   is-the-detector    this file IS the controls. A mutation to it cannot be caught by
#                      running it — that is circular. What protects it is the coverage
#                      table itself: delete a control and the count for the fix it
#                      covered drops, or the fix reports UNCOVERED.
#   content            not executable gate machinery. Covered by a different gate, named
#                      in the note. Reverting it fails THAT gate, not these controls.
